patent: Published application US 2017/0106964 A1, The Boeing Company, filed 2015-10-14, published 2017-04-20. Google Patents lists the grant as US 9,926,066 B2 (2018-03-27); the claims here are those of the publication. Describes a fitting for the corner where beams intersect: a strap with a rounded semi-conical middle, clamped between a male and a female fitting, with two flat legs attached to the two beam webs. Load path [0056]: tension in a fastener, compression in the male fitting, hoop load in the strap radius, tension in the legs, shear into the webs. Two versions: FIG. 5-8 and FIG. 13-16. The described use is an aircraft floor; [0034] extends it to other vehicles and stationary structures. No aircraft program is named. The text gives tolerances (for example within 0.010 inch [0044], within ±5° [0043]) but no overall dimensions, ply counts or test data, and names fiber and resin only in its fiber-metal laminate examples [0048]. US 9,593,740 in this collection, also Boeing, lists inventors with the same names plus middle initials and describes a different fitting.

glossary.def: Part installed in the corner of a beam joint to carry an upward pull from a fastener into the beam webs [0002], [0033].
Web: the vertical plate of an I-beam. Flanges: the horizontal plates at its top and bottom [0032].
Half of a cone surface. Clamping the strap on it sets the legs to the corner angle [0043].
Tension running around a curved path, as in a ring [0056].
Load transferred along the attached face, here from strap leg to web [0056].
Tension across the thickness of a laminate, carried by the matrix, which is weaker than the fibers [0003]-[0004].
Ply: one layer of fiber in a polymer matrix. Layup: the stack of plies [0003].
Ply with its fibers running one way [0045]-[0046].
Plies at several angles, giving similar in-plane stiffness in all directions; mentioned in [0045].
Fiber plies pre-impregnated with resin before layup [0046].
Fibers shaped without resin, then filled with resin and cured [0048], [0066].
Co-cured: parts cured together. Co-bonded: a part bonded to another while one of them cures [0061].
Sealed under a film and evacuated to compact the part during cure [0075].
Glass laminate aluminum reinforced epoxy, a fiber-metal laminate [0048].
Coefficient of thermal expansion [0053].
External fitting with a walled recess, sized to receive a folded tie-down ring [0036].
Cross-section sheet between the back-to-back segments, joining adjacent webs [0064].
Area of increased flange thickness, here at the corners [0062].
Smooth flat seat around a fastener hole [0050].
The tail assembly of an aircraft [0030].
Rapid crushing load, the text's example being an aircraft impact event [0033].
